scenario.topic: Decide which programming language for a new internal tool
scenario.opening_question: What trade-offs are we willing to make between development speed, long-term maintenance, and team familiarity?

options.name: Python 3.10 with FastAPI Framework
options.upside: Rapid prototyping and easy integration with existing Python code
options.tradeoff: Moderate runtime performance might limit scalability under heavy load
options.concern: Some team members have limited experience with FastAPI specifics
options.best_for: fast development with maintainable, readable code

options.name: TypeScript with Node.js and Express
options.upside: Strong typing reduces bugs and team is very familiar with JavaScript ecosystem
options.tradeoff: Longer initial setup and boilerplate code slows early progress
options.concern: Potentially more complex deployment and dependency management
options.best_for: high performance and type safety with familiar tools

options.name: Go 1.20 with Gin Web Framework
options.upside: Excellent runtime performance and easy concurrency support
options.tradeoff: Steeper learning curve and slower initial development due to unfamiliarity
options.concern: Limited internal expertise could delay debugging and feature additions

options.name: Ruby 3.1 with Rails 7
options.upside: Convention-over-configuration accelerates development and rich libraries
options.tradeoff: Slower runtime and potential scaling challenges for heavy workloads
options.concern: Some team members have minimal Ruby experience, risking maintenance issues
options.best_for: quick feature delivery with rich built-in tools

shared_context: The internal tool must be ready within 3 months
The team consists of exactly 4 developers with mixed experience
The tool will be used by other internal teams and should be maintainable

personas.background: As a developer who values rapid feature delivery, Nico prefers tools that speed up development cycles even if performance is moderate.
